items.label: f01-three-questions
items.front: The validation/auth guide separates three questions. Name them and the Postiz mechanism behind each.
items.back: Validation (is the input well-formed?): the global ValidationPipe plus the manual pipe in mapTypeToPost, DTO sanitizers and magic-byte file checks. Authentication (who is this?): AuthMiddleware, a JWT from cookie or header, applied to listed controllers. Authorization (may they do this to that?): CASL plan/role gates via @CheckPolicies and PoliciesGuard, plus orgId in each repository where clause.

items.label: f04-poor-mans-outbox
items.front: Why does the side-effects guide call post scheduling a poor man's outbox, and what would a real one change?
items.back: createPost commits the post, then calls startWorkflow fire-and-forget with .catch(() => {}); a failed start is swallowed and only the periodic missing-post sweep repairs it. The row is the intent and the sweep the dispatcher. A transactional outbox writes the post and an outbox row in one transaction, and a dispatcher drains it, starts workflows and marks them sent.

items.label: f03-missing-post-sweep
items.front: What is the missing-post sweep, and when does it run?
items.back: A compensating workflow (missingPostWorkflow, id missing-post-workflow) that finds posts whose workflow start was lost and starts or pokes their post_<id> workflows. InfiniteWorkflowRegister starts it on module init only when RUN_CRON is set; with RUN_CRON unset, lost starts are never repaired (risk R17).

items.label: f02-workflow-idempotency
items.front: How does Postiz make scheduling a post idempotent with Temporal, and where is idempotency absent?
items.back: Each post's workflow has the deterministic id post_<postId>: startWorkflow uses workflowIdConflictPolicy TERMINATE_EXISTING (a reschedule replaces the run), and the missing-post sweep uses signalWithStart with USE_EXISTING (a running workflow is just poked). Absent: posting to the provider and outgoing webhooks, so a retry after a success can duplicate them.

items.prompt: POST /posts declares its body as @Body() rawBody: any. Where is that body validated against CreatePostDto?

choices.text: In mapTypeToPost, which runs a new ValidationPipe with CreatePostDto
In the global ValidationPipe, which reads the DTO type from the service
In PoliciesGuard, which validates the body before checking the plan
Nowhere: an any body is passed to createPost unvalidated

choices: In mapTypeToPost, which runs a new ValidationPipe with CreatePostDto
In the global ValidationPipe, which reads the DTO type from the service
In PoliciesGuard, which validates the body before checking the plan
Nowhere: an any body is passed to createPost unvalidated

items.explanation: The global pipe validates by metatype, and a param typed any has no DTO class, so it is skipped. The service's mapTypeToPost then builds new ValidationPipe({ transform: true, ... }) and calls transform(mappedValues, { metatype: CreatePostDto }): the duplicated second layer the guide describes.

items.prompt: A client creates a post for a LinkedIn integration but sends settings.__type = 'x'. Which __type does mapTypeToPost validate against?

choices.text: The integration's providerIdentifier, replacing the client's value
The client's 'x', so the X settings DTO is used to validate that post
Neither one: a mismatch between the two returns a 400 error
Both, applied one after the other, keeping whichever passes

choices: The integration's providerIdentifier, replacing the client's value
The client's 'x', so the X settings DTO is used to validate that post
Neither one: a mismatch between the two returns a 400 error
Both, applied one after the other, keeping whichever passes

items.explanation: For each post, mapTypeToPost loads the integration by org and id and returns settings: { ...post.settings, __type: integration.providerIdentifier }. The spread comes first, so the server value overwrites the client's. The discriminator then picks the settings class for the real provider.

items.prompt: How long is a JWT from AuthService.signJWT valid, and what does it carry?

choices.text: One hour, the jsonwebtoken default; it carries only the user id
Until logout, which adds its id to a Redis denylist; it carries the org
Seven days, as set by the JWT_EXPIRES setting; it carries the user id
Forever, as no expiresIn is passed; it carries the whole user object

choices: One hour, the jsonwebtoken default; it carries only the user id
Until logout, which adds its id to a Redis denylist; it carries the org
Seven days, as set by the JWT_EXPIRES setting; it carries the user id
Forever, as no expiresIn is passed; it carries the whole user object

items.explanation: signJWT is sign(value, process.env.JWT_SECRET!) with no options, so the token has no exp claim; jsonwebtoken has no default lifetime. The value signed is the user row passed in. With no expiry and no denylist there is no revocation, which is risk R6.

items.prompt: A post is submitted with type 'draft' and settings missing a field that the provider's settings DTO requires. What happens at validation?

choices.text: Validation fails, since class-validator always checks nested DTOs
The missing field gets its DTO default value and then validates
The post is converted to a schedule, and then validation fails
@ValidateIf skips the settings checks when the type is draft

choices: Validation fails, since class-validator always checks nested DTOs
The missing field gets its DTO default value and then validates
The post is converted to a schedule, and then validation fails
@ValidateIf skips the settings checks when the type is draft

items.explanation: settings carries @ValidateIf((o) => o.type !== 'draft') above @ValidateNested, so for a draft every validator on that property is skipped. The guide's table lists this as a thing a senior notices: drafts skip settings validation, so bad settings surface only when the draft is later scheduled.

items.prompt: A configured webhook URL is unreachable when a post is published. What does the sendWebhooks activity do?

choices.text: Writes a failed delivery row that the UI then shows on the webhook
Swallows the fetch error; the activity still completes normally
Signs the payload again and retries with exponential backoff
Throws, so Temporal retries the activity up to two more times

choices: Writes a failed delivery row that the UI then shows on the webhook
Swallows the fetch error; the activity still completes normally
Signs the payload again and retries with exponential backoff
Throws, so Temporal retries the activity up to two more times

items.explanation: Each delivery is await fetch(...) inside try { } catch (e) { /**empty**/ }, run under Promise.all, so a network error is discarded and the activity resolves. There is no signature, no retry and no delivery log; the side-effects guide grades webhooks D for exactly this.

items.prompt: setNickname ends in updateNameAndUrl(id, name, url), a write keyed by integration id alone. Why is it not an IDOR today?

choices.text: getIntegrationById(org.id, id) runs first and throws if not found
AuthMiddleware rejects any id that is not in the caller's JWT
The write is wrapped in a transaction that rolls back on mismatch
updateNameAndUrl adds the organization id to its where clause

choices: getIntegrationById(org.id, id) runs first and throws if not found
AuthMiddleware rejects any id that is not in the caller's JWT
The write is wrapped in a transaction that rolls back on mismatch
updateNameAndUrl adds the organization id to its where clause

items.explanation: Before any write, the controller loads the integration with the caller's org.id and the path id, and throws 'Invalid integration' when nothing comes back, so a foreign id never reaches the id-only update. The risk register calls this safe today, with the guard living in the caller rather than in the query.

items.prompt: A handler on an authenticated controller has no @CheckPolicies decorator. What does PoliciesGuard.canActivate return for it?

choices.text: true only on self-hosted installs; cloud installs deny it
false, as a handler with no policies is denied by default
true, as an empty policy list allows the request
It throws, as a gated controller needs policy metadata

choices: true only on self-hosted installs; cloud installs deny it
false, as a handler with no policies is denied by default
true, as an empty policy list allows the request
It throws, as a gated controller needs policy metadata

items.explanation: After the path-string shortcuts, the guard reads CHECK_POLICIES_KEY metadata with a default of [], and returns true when the list is empty. Self-hosting is checked later, inside the policy evaluation, so it does not matter here. Plan gating only happens for handlers that declare policies.

items.prompt: A developer adds a new controller to ApiModule's controllers array but forgets to add it to authenticatedController. What happens to its routes?

choices.text: AuthMiddleware still runs, as it is applied to the whole module
They are served without AuthMiddleware and its identity check
Nest refuses to boot, because the controller has no middleware
They answer 401 until the controller is put in the list

choices: AuthMiddleware still runs, as it is applied to the whole module
They are served without AuthMiddleware and its identity check
Nest refuses to boot, because the controller has no middleware
They answer 401 until the controller is put in the list

items.explanation: configure() applies AuthMiddleware with forRoutes(...authenticatedController), so only listed controllers get it. A controller registered outside that list is served with no identity check: the fail-open boundary the guides and risk R5 describe. Nest boots fine and returns no 401 by itself.

items.prompt: A scheduled post is edited and saved back as a DRAFT, so startWorkflow runs with state 'DRAFT'. What happens to its Temporal workflow?

choices.text: The running workflow gets a 'poke' signal to re-read the post state
A new post_<id> workflow starts and sleeps until the draft is published
The running workflow keeps going and publishes at its old time
Running workflows for the post are terminated, and none is started

choices: The running workflow gets a 'poke' signal to re-read the post state
A new post_<id> workflow starts and sleeps until the draft is published
The running workflow keeps going and publishes at its old time
Running workflows for the post are terminated, and none is started

items.explanation: startWorkflow first lists workflows with postId = this post and ExecutionStatus Running, terminating each one; then if state === 'DRAFT' it returns before workflow.start. The poke signal belongs to the missing-post sweep (signalWithStart), not this path.

items.prompt: A user in organization A sends PUT /posts/tags/:id with the id of a tag that belongs to organization B. What does editTag do?

choices.text: Fails with a not-found error, because orgId is part of the where
Is refused by PoliciesGuard before the repository method is ever run
Renames B's tag, since the update's where clause holds just the id
Creates a copy of the tag inside organization A with the new name

choices: Fails with a not-found error, because orgId is part of the where
Is refused by PoliciesGuard before the repository method is ever run
Renames B's tag, since the update's where clause holds just the id
Creates a copy of the tag inside organization A with the new name

items.explanation: posts.repository editTag accepts orgId but its update uses where: { id } alone, so any tag id is updated whatever organization owns it: an IDOR. deleteTag right below it does put orgId in the where. No copy is made, and the PoliciesGuard checks plan/role policies, not ownership.

items.prompt: A PDF is uploaded as photo.png with mimetype image/png. What does CustomFileValidationPipe do?

choices.text: Accepts it, but only when its size is under the image size limit
Accepts it, since image/png is on the allowed mimetype list
Rejects it as 'Unsupported file type.' from the sniffed bytes
Renames it to photo.pdf and stores it with the PDF mimetype

choices: Accepts it, but only when its size is under the image size limit
Accepts it, since image/png is on the allowed mimetype list
Rejects it as 'Unsupported file type.' from the sniffed bytes
Renames it to photo.pdf and stores it with the PDF mimetype

items.explanation: The pipe runs fromBuffer(value.buffer) to detect the type from the file's magic bytes and checks the detected mime against ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES; the client's mimetype and file name are never consulted. A PDF is detected as application/pdf, which is not in the set, so it throws BadRequestException('Unsupported file type.').

items.prompt: A post activity fails on every attempt. Under proxyTaskQueue's retry policy, how many times does it run, and how far apart?

choices.text: Unlimited attempts until the 10-minute timeout is reached
Three attempts in all, spaced a fixed 2 minutes apart
Five attempts, retried every 5 seconds by the provider fetch
Three attempts, with the gap doubling from 2 minutes each time

choices: Unlimited attempts until the 10-minute timeout is reached
Three attempts in all, spaced a fixed 2 minutes apart
Five attempts, retried every 5 seconds by the provider fetch
Three attempts, with the gap doubling from 2 minutes each time

items.explanation: retry is { maximumAttempts: 3, backoffCoefficient: 1, initialInterval: '2 minutes' }. A coefficient of 1 means the interval never grows. startToCloseTimeout ('10 minute') limits one attempt, not the retry series; the 5-second fetch retry and the 5-iteration refresh loop are separate layers.
